## Weekly Digest — 2026-07-15

### 1) What changed (last 7 days)
Nearly all activity was building **CRS Brain itself** (the app you're talking to), not the CRS product:
- **App shipped from zero → working:** initial CRS Brain app, streaming replies, model + reasoning-effort selectors, live usage panel, weekly digest, auto-commit.
- **Buildprint operational:** CLI linked, Test branch cloned, first audit ingested; Buildprint added as a full chat mode; runbook + `Bash(buildprint:*)` access.
- **Knowledge base loaded:** full Bubble manual (583 pages) + Buildprint manual (71 pages) + 87 curated forum threads with live-search fallback.
- **Brain Map** (galaxy visualization at `/map`), **Board** tile view, and **mobile access** (LAN + PIN gate).
- **Content work (thin):** 8-step Pattern A migration plan written to brain; 7 CRS sections listed; option-set table generated.

### 2) In progress now
- **Casino Settings RE** (reusable element) — the only item in the "now" column of the board (unchanged since 2026-05-02).
- **Batch 1 UI** (project-only file view + recent files) — latest commit, just landed.

### 3) What's next
- Board `next` column is **empty** — nothing queued.
- Deferred/`later`: **Report DT workflow optimization** (Day 2).

### 4) Missing / stalled / at risk
- **The actual CRS product hasn't moved in ~10 weeks.** Board still dated 2026-05-02; Casino Settings RE has been "in progress" the whole time. All 46 modules remain roadmap, nothing shipped.
- **Tooling has eaten the week.** ~90 commits, almost entirely on the second-brain app — risk of building the tool instead of the product.
- **May 31 live-cutover deadline** (per CLAUDE.md) is past with no sign of migration progress; Pattern A exists only as a plan.
- **Empty `next` queue** — no committed next action means the product side has no momentum.

**Blunt take:** the Brain is impressive infrastructure, but it's a productivity tool, not revenue. Casino Settings RE has been stuck for 2+ months. Pick one CRS module and finish it this week, or the tooling sprint becomes avoidance.

Want me to set a concrete `next` item on the board to break the stall?
